target_customer: Space agencies, universities and companies buying PocketQube launch rides and satellite platforms, and government and commercial imagery customers
problem: Small satellites lack affordable launch access and frequent revisit Earth observation is limited; Alba builds tiny satellites to image everywhere every 15 minutes.
business_model: Launch brokerage and satellite platform sales (PocketQube rides, Unicorn platform), with a planned imagery data service
product_category: PocketQube satellites, launch services and Earth observation

founders.name: Tom Walkinshaw
founders.background_notes: Named as founder and CEO in the TechCrunch seed coverage and in ESA material. Education and prior employers not found in a source opened. A directory lists Chris Larmour as co-founder but no company or YC source confirms this, so he is not listed.

competitors.name: Planet
competitors.traction_then: Operating a large constellation per the seed coverage

competitors.name: Satellite Vu
competitors.what: Orbital thermal imaging startup targeting night time observation

technical_complexity.rationale: Imaging payloads under 1 kg with orbital operations and launch integration, plus a deployer (Albapod) flown on multiple missions; hardware plus launch risk.

defensibility.rationale: Flight heritage across 11 missions and 62 PocketQubes and a deployer product give an edge in a niche format, but few customers and larger satellite makers can adapt.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found of incumbents copying the PocketQube format. The CEO said in the 2021 coverage that Alba had more time invested in this class of satellite than anyone else.

market_need_then: Seed coverage cites demand for night time and frequent revisit imaging and notes competitor Satellite Vu raised 5M USD for the same idea. The company later claims over 85M USD of LOIs, which is its own statement.

identity.visual_style: Space hardware brand with Scottish identity
identity.voice_and_tone: Democratizing access to space, accessible and playful

branding.brand_signature: Unicorn satellites named after Scotland's national animal; the CEO said Scotland is the only country to have chosen a mythical creature as its symbol
branding.community_and_virality: Regional press coverage in Scotland and ESA features of the Unicorn satellites; no merch or fan community found

brand_strength.rationale: Memorable product naming and steady regional and ESA press, but a small niche audience.

outcome_analysis: Alba Orbital raised a 3.4M USD seed in May 2021 after YC and has since flown 62 PocketQubes across 11 missions, giving real flight heritage. It remains active with about ten people and a claimed LOI pipeline, but the 15 minute imaging constellation is still ahead of it, so outcome rests on future launches and funding that are not yet public.
notes: Seed amount confirmed by TechCrunch and eeNews Europe; Tech.eu lists 2.8M EUR. CB Insights shows a later seed in 2023-01 and 3.53M USD total, not confirmed elsewhere, so it is not recorded. A 100K GBP Scottish Enterprise grant for Albapod V3 is mentioned on the company site with no date, so not recorded as a round. Founded year 2012 comes from encyclopedia style sources and may not match the YC listing. Outcome search found no launch failures, layoffs or sale involving Alba. Name origin of Alba itself not found.
